records.name: Lyrics
prompts: Pick up a book. Open it to a random page. Write an entire song using only lines from that page.
Write a verse where every line starts with the same word.
Write a song about the room you're sitting in right now. Be specific.
Take the last conversation you had. Turn it into a chorus.
Write a verse with no adjectives. Only nouns and verbs.
Write a love song that never uses the word "love".
Open your phone notes. Find the last thing you wrote. Build a verse around it.
Write a verse where each line is shorter than the one before it.

records.name: Melody
prompts: Sing the first thing that comes into your head. Record it. That's your melody.
Take the last 4 notes you played. Reverse them. Build a melody from that.
Hum a melody using only 3 notes. When you find one you like, add a 4th.
Play a scale you never use. Find a melody hiding inside it.
Sing a melody to the rhythm of your name.
Play any chord. Hum a note that ISN'T in it. Start your melody there.
Write a melody that only moves by steps — no leaps. Then add one leap at the end.

records.name: Riff
prompts: Play one string. One fret. Repeat it until it becomes a riff.
Take a rhythm from a song you hate. Steal it. Change the notes.
Play a power chord. Move it one fret up. Then one more. That's your riff.
Use only the top two strings. Find a riff in 4 notes.
Play a riff entirely on harmonics.
Take a vocal melody you know. Play it on one string. Speed it up.
Play 3 notes. Stop. Reverse them. Repeat until it grooves.

records.name: Chords
prompts: Play a chord you've never played before. Write a song around it.
Take a progression you know. Change one chord to something "wrong". Keep it.
Write a verse using only two chords. The tension IS the point.
Play a chord. Move one finger. That's your next chord. Move again.
Write a progression that never resolves. Sit in the suspense.
Take the saddest chord you know. Make it the chorus.
Use only chords with no root note. Let the bass define the key.

records.name: Rhythm
prompts: Tap a rhythm on your knee. Don't think. Just tap for 30 seconds. Steal the best part.
Write a riff using only one note. All the variation is in the rhythm.
Take a heartbeat rhythm. Speed it up. Slow it down. Find where it grooves.
Play a rhythm in 3/4. Then play the same pattern in 4/4.
Mute all strings. Strum a rhythm with no notes. When it feels good, add one chord.
Write a drum pattern in your head. Transfer it to guitar — bass notes for kick, high strings for snire.

records.name: Structure
prompts: Write a song with no chorus. Just verses. Each one slightly different.
Write a song that's one long crescendo. Start quiet. End loud.
Write a 30-second song. No more, no less.
Write a song that loops — the end connects back to the beginning.
Write a verse, then skip the chorus. Go straight to a bridge. Then end.
Write three sections: statement, contradiction, resolution.

records.name: Mood
prompts: Close your eyes. Picture a colour. Write the song that colour sounds like.
Write the saddest thing you can. Then remove all the sad words.
Write a song for 3am. Not sad, not happy. Just awake.
Write a song that feels like driving at night.
Write a song that scares you a little.
Write a lullaby for yourself.

records.name: Wildcard
prompts: Roll a die. That's how many chords you're allowed to use.
Flip a coin. Heads: major key. Tails: minor key. Now write.
Pick a random object in the room. It's your song title. Go.
Text a friend: "Give me a song title". Write it before they reply.
Set a timer for 10 minutes. Write a complete song. Don't stop.
Play the first chord that comes to you. Don't change it for the whole song.
Write a song in a genre you've never listened to. Go on instinct.
